_about: Tidal play spots, seeded into river_runs by scripts/add_tidal_runs.py. Flows are max flood current in knots, from Skook Surfing's wave guide (skooksurfing.com) until the person confirms. Pins marked in pinNote are approximate. After seeding, edit in the Firebase console; this file is only the starting copy.

skookumchuck-narrows.name: Skookumchuck Narrows - Skook
skookumchuck-narrows.description: Sechelt Rapids, the tidal playwave at Roland Point in Skookumchuck Narrows Provincial Park. The main wave forms on the flood, so plan on the max flood: its time and its speed in knots. Ebbs don't make the wave. The ebb before a flood should be close to the flood's speed for a good wave; a much smaller ebb usually means a higher tide and a weaker wave.
skookumchuck-narrows.hazards: Big boils and whirlpools downstream, growing fast above about 13 kt. Bring a bombproof roll: rescues here are long. Above 15 kt (Big Skook) it's experts only.
skookumchuck-narrows.access: Hike about 4 km from the Skookumchuck Narrows trailhead in Egmont to Roland Point, or paddle from Egmont. Time the trip around slack water.
skookumchuck-narrows.pinNote: Put-in pin at the trailhead is approximate; the run pin is the CHS Sechelt Rapids current station at Roland Point.

flowRanges.note: Max flood. 7 to 10 kt is a sea kayak wave; 10 to 15 kt is the whitewater wave (Class III paddlers start at 9 to 11 kt); 15 to 18 kt is Big Skook, experts only.
